items.name: Collapse Construct
items.summary: You've modified your construct companion and built it out of light materials, enabling you to collapse it into a carrying case or other compact and innocuous form.
items.description:
You've modified your construct companion and built it out of light materials, enabling you to collapse it into a carrying case or other compact and innocuous form. Either your construct or you (if you're adjacent to it) can Collapse your Construct to turn it into its compact form or back into its normal form.

In compact form, your construct can't act but is easily carried, with a Bulk of 2 if it's Small, 4 if it's Medium, or 8 if it's Large. The compact form has wheels, so you can easily drag it behind you at half your Speed (rather than the usual slower Speed for dragging).

items.name: Reverse Engineer
items.summary: You are incredibly skilled at reverse engineering items to learn their formulas or disassembling them just to disable them.
items.description:
You are incredibly skilled at reverse engineering items to learn their formulas or disassembling them just to disable them. If you are using the Critical Crafting alternate rules and you get a critical success on your Crafting check to reverse engineer an item, you can reassemble the original item with one of the critical success crafting benefits (as determined by your GM).

Furthermore, you can use Crafting instead of Thievery to Disable Device or Pick A Lock.

items.name: Searing Restoration
items.summary: They told you there was no way that explosions could heal people, but they were fools… Fools who didn't understand your brilliance!
items.description:
They told you there was no way that explosions could heal people, but they were fools… Fools who didn't understand your brilliance! You create a minor explosion from your innovation, altering the combustion to cauterize wounds using vaporized medicinal herbs. You or a living creature adjacent to you regains level-based Hit Points. In addition, the creature you heal can attempt an immediate flat check to recover from a single source of persistent bleed damage, with the DC reduction from appropriate assistance.

At 3rd level, and every 2 levels thereafter, increase the healing by 1d10.

**Special** If your innovation is a minion, it can take this action rather than you, though because it's not a living creature, it can't use the ability on itself.

items.name: Advanced Construct Companion
items.summary: You've upgraded your construct companion's power and decision-making ability.
items.description: You've upgraded your construct companion's power and decision-making ability. It becomes an advanced construct companion. During an encounter, even if you don't use the Command a Construct action, your construct companion can still use 1 action on your turn that round to Stride or Strike.
items.cite: Guns & Gears (Remastered) — Feats: Advanced Construct Companion

items.name: Diving Armor
items.summary: You've modified your armor with fins, rotors, and other devices to make it easy for you to move through the water, plus mechanical gills that can help you extract breathable air from water.
items.description: You've modified your armor with fins, rotors, and other devices to make it easy for you to move through the water, plus mechanical gills that can help you extract breathable air from water. While wearing your armor innovation, you can breathe underwater and gain a swim Speed equal to your land Speed.

items.name: Dual-Form Weapon
items.summary: Your innovation has replaceable interlocking pieces that you can use to transform it into another type of weapon.
items.description:
Your innovation has replaceable interlocking pieces that you can use to transform it into another type of weapon. When you select this feat, choose a level 0 weapon. It must be either a common weapon or another to which you have access. This weapon becomes your innovation's second configuration.

Select a new set of weapon modifications for this new configuration. You can spend two Interact actions to switch your weapon innovation between the two configurations. These actions don't need to be taken consecutively, but if you've provided the first and not the second, the weapon is non-functional as it is stranded between states. Your weapon's Bulk is always the greater Bulk of the two configurations, regardless of which configuration it's in—if one weapon is smaller than the other, you still need to keep any weapon parts on hand. Any runes on your weapon innovation affect the second weapon configuration as long as it would normally qualify for them.

items.name: Gadget Specialist
items.summary: Rather than just using your gadgets for various boosts and tweaks, you also craft a few specific temporary consumable gadgets each day.
items.description:
Rather than just using your gadgets for various boosts and tweaks, you also craft a few specific temporary consumable gadgets each day. You gain the formulas for three common or uncommon gadgets. Each day during your daily preparations, you can create two temporary gadgets from your formula book. Gadgets prepared in this way don't cost you any resources to Craft and don't have any sale value. They are temporary items and fall apart the next time you make your daily preparations if you haven't already used them.

If you're a master in Crafting, you can create three gadgets per day, and you gain three additional common or uncommon gadget formulas. If you're legendary in Crafting, you can create four gadgets per day, and you gain another additional three common or uncommon gadget formulas, for a total of nine.

items.name: Megaton Strike
items.summary: You activate gears, explosives, and other hidden mechanisms in your innovation to make a powerful attack.
items.description:
You activate gears, explosives, and other hidden mechanisms in your innovation to make a powerful attack. You make a Strike, dealing an extra die of weapon damage. If you're at least 10th level, increase this to two extra dice, and if you're at least 18th level, increase it to three extra dice. The type of Strike you can make depends on your innovation.

- **Armor** You Strike with a melee unarmed attack or a melee weapon. To use a melee weapon for this, you must have prepared it in advance with special contraptions when you make your daily preparations.
- **Construct** Your minion innovation Strikes.
- **Weapon** You Strike with your weapon innovation.

**Unstable Function** You put even more force into the Strike, though you risk stress fractures to your innovation. Add the unstable trait to Megaton Strike. The Strike deals another extra damage die, for a total of two extra dice at 4th level, three at 10th level, and four at 18th level.

**Special** If your innovation is a minion, it can take this action rather than you.

items.name: Clockwork Celerity
items.summary: You can use unstable clockwork devices in your innovation to push your invention to act more quickly.
items.description:
**Trigger** Your turn begins.

You can use unstable clockwork devices in your innovation to push your invention to act more quickly. You are quickened for this turn. How you can use the extra action depends on your innovation.

- **Armor** You can use the extra action to Step, Stride, or use another movement action granted by your innovation (such as Swim if you have the Diving Armor feat).
- **Construct** You can use the extra action to Command your construct innovation (or to provide 1 of the actions if you spend 2 actions to Command your construct).
- **Weapon** You can use the extra action to Strike with your innovation or Reload your innovation.

items.name: Construct Shell
items.summary: You've adjusted your construct innovation so that when you ride it, special plates, hollows, or similar form partial barriers around you to add additional protection.
items.description:
You've adjusted your construct innovation so that when you ride it, special plates, hollows, or similar form partial barriers around you to add additional protection. You have lesser cover from all attacks when mounted on your construct innovation, not just from attacks where the construct would be in the way.

Additionally, if your construct uses an emanation while you're riding on it, such as Explode, you can choose not to be affected by the emanation.

items.name: Megavolt
items.summary: You bleed off some electric power from your innovation in the shape of a damaging bolt.
items.description:
You bleed off some electric power from your innovation in the shape of a damaging bolt. Creatures in a 20-foot line from your innovation take level-based electricity damage, with a basic Reflex against your class DC. The electricity damage increases by 1d4 at 8th level and every 2 levels thereafter.

**Unstable Function** You overload and supercharge the voltage even higher. Add the unstable trait to Megavolt. The area increases to a 60-foot line and the damage increases from d4s to d12s. If you have the breakthrough innovation class feature, you can choose a 60-foot or 90-foot line for the area when you use an unstable Megavolt; if you also have the revolutionary innovation class feature, you can choose a 60-foot, 90-foot, or 120-foot line.

**Special** If your innovation is a minion, it can take this action rather than you.

items.name: Visual Fidelity
items.summary: You've found a way to use a hodgepodge combination of devices to enhance your visual abilities in every situation.
items.description:
You've found a way to use a hodgepodge combination of devices to enhance your visual abilities in every situation. You gain darkvision and low-light vision, and you can see invisible creatures and objects as translucent shapes, though these shapes are indistinct enough to be concealed to you.

If an effect would give you the blinded condition, the effect must attempt a counteract check against your class DC, with your counteract rank equaling half your level, rounded up. On a failed counteract check, you aren't blinded-your various devices are able to compensate.

items.name: Gigaton Strike
items.summary: When you use a full-power Megaton Strike, you can knock your foe back.
items.description:
When you use a full-power Megaton Strike, you can knock your foe back. When you succeed at your Strike while using an unstable Megaton Strike, your target must attempt a Fortitude save against your class DC.

**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.

**Success** The creature is pushed back 5 feet.

**Failure** The creature is pushed back 10 feet.

**Critical Failure** The creature is pushed back 20 feet.

**Special** If your innovation is a minion, this benefit applies on its unstable Megaton Strikes.

items.name: Incredible Construct Companion
items.summary: Thanks to your continual tinkering, your construct companion has advanced to an astounding new stage of engineering, enhancing all its attributes.
items.description: Thanks to your continual tinkering, your construct companion has advanced to an astounding new stage of engineering, enhancing all its attributes. Your construct companion becomes an incredible construct companion.
items.cite: Guns & Gears (Remastered) — Feats: Incredible Construct Companion

items.name: Manifold Modifications
items.summary: You've modified your innovation using clever workarounds, so you can include another initial modification without compromising its structure.
items.description: You've modified your innovation using clever workarounds, so you can include another initial modification without compromising its structure. Your innovation gains an additional initial modification from the list for innovations of its type.

items.name: Overdrive Ally
items.summary: You quickly fling some of your powered-up mechanisms to an ally, sharing your benefits with them briefly.
items.description:
**Requirements** You are currently in overdrive.

You quickly fling some of your powered-up mechanisms to an ally, sharing your benefits with them briefly. Choose an ally within 30 feet. Until the end of their next turn, that ally's Strikes deal additional damage equal to half your Intelligence modifier, or your full Intelligence modifier if you were in critical overdrive. The ally doesn't gain the increased damage from expert, master, or legendary overdrive.

Effect: Overdrive Ally

items.name: Ubiquitous Gadgets
items.summary: They thought you had used up all your devices, but they thought wrong!
items.description:
They thought you had used up all your devices, but they thought wrong! You have a few more gadgets up your sleeve than others expect. Increase the number of temporary gadgets you can create each day by 2.

**Special** You can select this feat a second time if you are 14th level or higher.

items.name: Distracting Explosion
items.summary: Your enemies think they can concentrate on something else while you're nearby?
items.description:
**Trigger** A creature within your reach uses a concentrate action.

Your enemies think they can concentrate on something else while you're nearby? Oh, you'll give them a distraction, all right! Make a melee Strike against the triggering creature with a weapon or unarmed attack that is benefiting from your offensive boost. This Strike doesn't count toward your multiple attack penalty, and your multiple attack penalty doesn't apply to this Strike.

**Unstable Function** You pull out all the stops to create an explosive distraction. Add the unstable trait to Distracting Explosion. If the attack hits, you disrupt the triggering concentrate action.

**Special** If your innovation is a minion, it can take this reaction instead of you, even though minions can't normally take reactions or act when it's not their turn. It uses your reaction for the turn to do so.

items.name: Electrify Armor
items.summary: You electrify your armor to punish foes who dare to attack you.
items.description:
**Requirements** You are wearing your armor innovation.

You electrify your armor to punish foes who dare to attack you. For 1 round, any creature that touches you, or that hits you with a melee unarmed attack or a non-reach melee weapon attack, takes 1d4 electricity damage. The effect ends if you cease wearing your armor innovation.

If you have the revolutionary innovation class feature, the damage increases to 2d4.

**Unstable Function** You create an unstable chain reaction, sending countless sparks dancing across your armor. Add the unstable trait to Electrify Armor. The effects last for 1 minute instead of 1 round, and the damage dice increase from d4s to d12s.

items.name: Helpful Tinkering
items.summary: You don't just tinker with your own innovation, you fiddle with your allies' weapons as well (for their benefit, of course).
items.description:
**Frequency** once per 10 minutes

You don't just tinker with your own innovation, you fiddle with your allies' weapons as well (for their benefit, of course). Choose an ally in your reach and one of their weapons. Attempt a Crafting check against a high DC for your level.

**Success** For 1 minute, the chosen ally's Strikes with the chosen weapon gain the same offensive boost your innovation has.

Effect: Helpful Tinkering

**Critical Failure** Your ally takes damage of the type and amount that your offensive boost normally deals on a successful Strike.

items.name: Lock On
items.summary: Aha!
items.description:
Aha! You lock on to your enemy's weak point to assist your construct companion in destroying it. When you Lock On, designate an enemy you can see. If your next action is to Command your construct, the construct gains a +2 circumstance bonus to attack rolls against the designated enemy until the end of the turn. If you use 2 actions for the Command, the bonus is instead a +3 circumstance bonus, or a +4 circumstance bonus if you're legendary in Crafting.

Effect: Lock On

items.name: Boost Modulation
items.summary: You aren't satisfied with keeping to just one kind of boost from your constant tinkering, so you've learned to modulate between several possibilities at once.
items.description: You aren't satisfied with keeping to just one kind of boost from your constant tinkering, so you've learned to modulate between several possibilities at once. Choose two additional offensive boosts. You can use an Interact action to change the offensive boost currently affecting your weapon, choosing between the one you chose for the class feature and the two you chose for this modification. If your weapon has the modular trait, you can swap the offensive boost as part of the Interact action you take to use that trait.

items.name: Contingency Gadgets
items.summary: You are too brilliant to be caught off guard, and you always have just the right gadget for the situation.
items.description:
You are too brilliant to be caught off guard, and you always have just the right gadget for the situation. When you prepare your gadgets during your daily preparations, you can choose to leave one of them as a contingency gadget that you keep ready for just this situation, rather than declaring which gadget you're making. You can pull the contingency gadget out using an Interact action, at which point you must choose which gadget you had prepared as a contingency.

If you're legendary in Crafting, you can leave two contingency gadgets during your daily preparations, instead of just one.

items.name: Deep Freeze
items.summary: You vent a jet of supercooled fluid from your innovation, damaging a foe and slowing it down.
items.description:
You vent a jet of supercooled fluid from your innovation, damaging a foe and slowing it down. Target one creature within 60 feet. That creature takes cold damage equal to your level, with effects depending on its Reflex save.

**Critical Success** The target is unaffected.

**Success** The target takes half damage and takes a –5-foot status penalty to its Speeds for 1 round.

**Failure** The target takes full damage and takes a –10-foot status penalty to its Speeds for 1 round.

**Critical Failure** The target takes double damage, is Slowed 1 for 1 round, and takes a –15-foot status penalty to its Speeds for 1 round.

Effect: Deep Freeze

**Unstable Function** Your innovation discharges an enormous cone of supercooled fluid, potentially causing cascading failures. Add the unstable trait to Deep Freeze. The ability affects all creatures within a 60-foot cone instead of a single target, and it deals cold damage equal to double your level instead of equal to your level.

If you have the revolutionary innovation class feature, you can choose a 60-foot cone or a 90-foot cone when you use an unstable Deep Freeze.

**Special** If your innovation is a minion, it can take this action rather than you.

items.name: Gigavolt
items.summary: When you unleash electricity from your innovation, you can bounce it off obstacles, creating a field of electric death.
items.description: When you unleash electricity from your innovation, you can bounce it off obstacles, creating a field of electric death. When you use Megavolt, each time your line of electricity hits a solid barrier, such as a wall, it bounces off at an angle of your choice and continues until you have reached the full length of the line. Even if a creature is in the area from multiple bounces, it takes the damage only once.

items.name: Shared Overdrive
items.summary: You've experimented enough on your teammates to transfer a substantial number of powered-up gizmos to them, enabling one of your allies to benefit from the full effects and duration of your Overdrive.
items.description:
You've experimented enough on your teammates to transfer a substantial number of powered-up gizmos to them, enabling one of your allies to benefit from the full effects and duration of your Overdrive. The first time you use Overdrive Ally during a given Overdrive, the effect lasts for the remainder of the duration of your Overdrive, instead of just until the end of the target's next turn. Any further uses of Overdrive Ally during the same Overdrive have their normal duration, per Overdrive Ally.

Effect: Overdrive Ally (Shared Overdrive)

items.name: Explosive Maneuver
items.summary: Thanks to a hidden experimental feature you built into your weapon, your weapon explosively deploys levers, tangling hooks, or similar mechanisms to provide significant assistance when you perform a…
items.description:
**Requirements** Your last action was a successful Strike against a foe using your weapon innovation.

Thanks to a hidden experimental feature you built into your weapon, your weapon explosively deploys levers, tangling hooks, or similar mechanisms to provide significant assistance when you perform a combat maneuver. When you use Explosive Maneuver, choose Grapple, Shove, or Trip. Your weapon innovation must have a weapon trait that matches the action you chose (for instance, to choose Grapple, your weapon must have the grapple trait). You take the chosen action against the same foe as your previous successful Strike, using the same multiple attack penalty as your previous successful Strike. You still increase your multiple attack penalty after the Grapple, Shove, or Trip, as normal.

items.name: Paragon Companion
items.summary: Your construct companion has reached the pinnacle of form and function.
items.description: Your construct companion has reached the pinnacle of form and function. Your construct companion becomes a paragon construct companion.

items.name: Soaring Armor
items.summary: Whether through a release of jets of flame, propeller blades, sonic bursts, streamlined aerodynamic structure, electromagnetic fields, or some combination of the above, you've managed to free your…
items.description: Whether through a release of jets of flame, propeller blades, sonic bursts, streamlined aerodynamic structure, electromagnetic fields, or some combination of the above, you've managed to free your innovation from the bonds of gravity! While wearing your innovation, you gain a fly Speed equal to your land Speed.

items.name: Unstable Redundancies
items.summary: You've built triple redundancies into your innovation and added all sorts of buffers to protect it from the harm of your unstable experiments.
items.description:
**Trigger** You would attempt the flat check for an unstable action, but you haven't rolled the flat check yet.

You've built triple redundancies into your innovation and added all sorts of buffers to protect it from the harm of your unstable experiments. You automatically succeed at the triggering flat check.

You can't rely on your Unstable Redundancies again until you spend 10 minutes setting them back up. If you spend 10 minutes retuning your innovation so you can use unstable actions again, you can set up your Unstable Redundancies during the same time.

items.name: Just the Thing!
items.summary: Need to balance on a razor's edge, force open an iron door, or persuade a dragon to negotiate?
items.description:
**Frequency** once per hour

Need to balance on a razor's edge, force open an iron door, or persuade a dragon to negotiate? Never fear! No matter the situation, you always have just the thing. You attempt a skill action that takes 1 minute or less to complete, using the same number of actions or amount of time as normal. However, as you take the action, describe a device you pull out and use to accomplish the skill. The specifics of how you accomplish this are up to you, but they should fit the challenge at hand. For instance, you might use gravitic stabilizers to balance on the razor's edge, a force battering ram gizmo to open the iron door, or a device that produces an aroma with the ability to pacify wyrms to persuade the dragon. Using an invention in this way lets you alter how you calculate the skill check used in the action. Instead of the normal skill modifier associated with that skill action, you use your Crafting modifier.
items.cite: Guns & Gears (Remastered) — Feats: Just the Thing!

items.name: Persistent Boost
items.summary: Your innovation sets foes on fire, covers them in acid, leaves barbed thorns behind, or otherwise deals persistent damage to your foes that sticks around long after you deliver your boosted attack.
items.description: Your innovation sets foes on fire, covers them in acid, leaves barbed thorns behind, or otherwise deals persistent damage to your foes that sticks around long after you deliver your boosted attack. When you or your construct innovation damage a foe with offensive boost, that foe also takes 1d8 persistent damage of the same damage type as the offensive boost damage.

items.name: You Failed to Account For... This!
items.summary: When your foes try to attack you, you always seem to have some outlandish invention you can pull out at the last second to protect you from whatever attack they throw at you.
items.description:
**Trigger** A creature you can see targets you with an attack against your AC.

When your foes try to attack you, you always seem to have some outlandish invention you can pull out at the last second to protect you from whatever attack they throw at you. Describe a device you're attempting to use to protect yourself from the foe's attack—for instance, when attacked by an elemental hurricane's lightning lash Strike, you might pull out a specially grounded lightning rod from that time you tried to power an invention by harnessing a thunderstorm! Using an invention to defend in this way means that the attack roll for the triggering attack targets your Crafting DC instead of your AC.

Since you're using your Crafting DC instead of your AC, any penalties to your AC don't apply, but this doesn't remove any conditions or other effects that are causing you such penalties. For instance, if you were off-guard and used an invention to defend against a sneak attack, you'd still take the extra precision damage if you were hit, even though the –2 penalty to AC from being off-guard wouldn't apply to your Crafting DC.
items.cite: Guns & Gears (Remastered) — Feats: You Failed to Account For... This!

items.name: Devastating Weaponry
items.summary: You release a volley of projectiles from your weapon, or power it to fly in every direction across the battlefield and Strike multiple creatures.
items.description: You release a volley of projectiles from your weapon, or power it to fly in every direction across the battlefield and Strike multiple creatures. Make a Strike with your weapon innovation against each foe within 30 feet of you. Don't increase your multiple attack penalty until after making all the attacks. If your innovation is a melee weapon and any of the attacks are outside your reach, you Release the weapon before the Strikes, and it returns to your grasp after all of them. If your hands are full when the weapon returns, it falls to the ground in your space. As normal, if your weapon innovation requires one or more actions to reload between Strikes, you can't use it to make multiple attacks with Devastating Weaponry.

items.name: Engine of Destruction
items.summary: Your construct unleashes a broad swath of devastation by separating its limbs, deploying hidden armaments, or using a similar technique to wreak havoc.
items.description:
Your construct unleashes a broad swath of devastation by separating its limbs, deploying hidden armaments, or using a similar technique to wreak havoc. You Command your innovation. Instead of its normal actions, it Strides once, then makes a Strike against each foe within 30 feet of it with a +2 circumstance bonus to its attack rolls. The multiple attack penalty doesn't increase until after the construct makes all the attacks.

Effect: Engine of Destruction
items.cite: Guns & Gears (Remastered) — Feats: Engine of Destruction

items.name: Negate Damage
items.summary: Your armor innovation activates various devices you prepared ahead of time, and you use one of them to reduce the damage you would take by 15.
items.description:
**Trigger** You would take damage.

Your armor innovation activates various devices you prepared ahead of time, and you use one of them to reduce the damage you would take by 15.

**Unstable Function** You activate all the precautions at once, violently repelling the incoming attack to blunt its force. Add the unstable trait to Negate Damage and reduce the damage you would take by 50.

items.name: Full Automation
items.summary: You become so entwined with your innovations that you can use them without a second thought.
items.description:
You become so entwined with your innovations that you can use them without a second thought. You're permanently quickened. How you can use the extra action depends on your innovation.

- **Armor** Your armor responds to the most subtle stimuli to move you in the right direction as long as you are wearing it. You can use the extra action to Stride, Step, or use a form of movement provided by your innovation (such as Fly or Swim).
- **Construct** Your ability to command your construct becomes instinctive. You can use the extra action to Command your construct innovation (or to provide 1 of the actions if you choose to spend 2 actions to Command your construct).
- **Weapon** Your weapon becomes easier to wield with deadly efficacy, almost as if it is an extension of your body. It speeds effortlessly toward whatever target you choose as long as you are holding it. You can use the extra action to Strike with your innovation.

items.name: Ubiquitous Overdrive
items.summary: You prepare a variety of incredible gizmos on each of your allies, linking them together through careful modification to enable you to power them up all at once.
items.description: You prepare a variety of incredible gizmos on each of your allies, linking them together through careful modification to enable you to power them up all at once. During your daily preparations, select up to six willing allies. Whenever you Overdrive, you grant the benefits of your overdrive to any of these allies you choose who are within 30 feet of you. The allies don't gain the increased damage from expert, master, or legendary overdrive.

items.name: Arcane Fists
items.summary: Your physical training encompasses unarmed combat forms.
items.description: Your physical training encompasses unarmed combat forms. The damage die for your fist changes to 1d6 instead of 1d4. You don't take the normal –2 circumstance penalty when making a lethal attack with your fist or any other unarmed attacks. Your unarmed attacks gain the arcane trait, making them magical. At 5th level, you also gain the critical specialization effects of unarmed attacks in the brawling group and weapons in the brawling group, using your spell DC instead of class DC.

items.name: Magus's Analysis
items.summary: You make an assessment informed by your knowledge of how a creature fights.
items.description: You make an assessment informed by your knowledge of how a creature fights. Attempt a check to Recall Knowledge about a creature, then recharge your Spellstrike. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to your check if you previously hit the creature with a Strike this turn. The subject of your check is temporarily immune to Magus's Analysis for 1 day.

items.name: Raise a Tome
items.summary: You can flip open a book to simultaneously study and deflect attacks.
items.description:
You can flip open a book to simultaneously study and deflect attacks. When you Raise a Shield, you can raise a book you're wielding instead of a shield. While you have a book raised, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to AC and a +1 circumstance bonus to Recall Knowledge checks to identify creatures using a skill related to the subject of the book (Arcana if you're using your spellbook). If consulting the book normally grants an item bonus to the check for consulting the book, you gain this bonus as well.

If you have Shield Block, you can use a raised tome for that feat as though it were a shield. The tome has Hardness 3, HP 12, and BT 6.

In addition, you can inscribe the *reinforcing* rune into your spellbook to strengthen your tomes, using the same process as transferring a rune. The rune takes the form of a specialized diagram in your spellbook, occupying one page. The rune's benefits apply to any one tome in your possession chosen during your daily preparations. If your spellbook leaves your possession, the rune-granting benefit is suppressed until you get the book back.
items.cite: Impossible Magic — Feats: Raise a Tome

items.name: Expansive Spellstrike
items.summary: You can blast the energy of a spell out around the target of your attack.
items.description: You can blast the energy of a spell out around the target of your attack. When you Spellstrike with a spell that has an area of a burst, cone, or line, the spell creates an area instead of affecting only the target. The target must be in the area, and Expansive Spellstrike has no effect if your spell was disrupted (such as if you critically fail your Strike). A burst is centered on any corner you choose of the target's square (or the corner of any square in its space for a Large or larger creature). A cone or line emits from you and must include the target; if you're not adjacent to the target (using a reach weapon or starlit span, for example), choose any square adjacent to the target as the source. The spell affects all creatures in the area as normal, but the Strike still targets only one creature.

items.name: Force Fang
items.summary: You can turn your attack into an unerring blur of force.
items.description: You can turn your attack into an unerring blur of force. You learn the Force Fang conflux spell.

items.name: Spirit Sheath
items.summary: You've magically constructed an extradimensional sheath for your weapon that you access through your clothing, typically through a pocket, sleeve, or seam.
items.description:
You've magically constructed an extradimensional sheath for your weapon that you access through your clothing, typically through a pocket, sleeve, or seam. This sheath is hard to notice, granting a +2 circumstance bonus to your Stealth checks to Conceal an Item within it. A spirit sheath can hold up to 1 Bulk worth of weapons.

During a Spellstrike, you can Interact to draw one weapon from the sheath before you Cast the Spell. You can draw or return a weapon to a spirit sheath as an Interact action, as can anyone else holding or wearing the clothing that contains the sheath. A Dispel Magic spell or similar effect can be used against the spirit sheath to expel the weapon. The counteract check is made against your spell DC and the counteract rank is half your level rounded up. The weapon is also expelled if you become unconscious.

items.name: Burning Cascade
items.summary: Energy flares out around you when you drop into your signature stance.
items.description: Energy flares out around you when you drop into your signature stance. When you use Arcane Cascade, each enemy in a 5-foot emanation takes damage equal to the extra damage from Arcane Cascade. This damage is the same type as that of Arcane Cascade. A creature that takes this damage is temporarily immune to further uses of Burning Cascade for 1 minute.

items.name: Devastating Spellstrike
items.summary: Your Spellstrike sweeps are so wide and devastating, they smash into nearby foes.
items.description:
**Requirements** Your Spellstrike is charged.

Your Spellstrike sweeps are so wide and devastating, they smash into nearby foes. Make a Spellstrike with a spell that can deal damage. Enemies in a 5-foot emanation around the target (not including the target) take 2 damage of the same damage type your spell could deal. This damage increases to 3 at 9th level, 4 at 14th level, and 5 at 19th level.

If you're in the Arcane Cascade stance, the emanation's damage gains a status bonus to damage equal to the extra damage from your Arcane Cascade.

items.name: Distracting Spellstrike
items.summary: You weave distracting magic with one hand to enhance the efficacy of your Spellstrike.
items.description:
**Requirements** You have a hand free, and your Spellstrike is charged.

You weave distracting magic with one hand to enhance the efficacy of your Spellstrike. Make a Spellstrike and Feint against the target of your Strike. Execute your Feint immediately before making the Strike, but after choosing your target. The Feint gains the arcane and visual traits, and it always has the basic effects of a Feint, rather than applying any adjustments or alternate effects from other feats or abilities.

If you're in the Arcane Cascade stance, you gain a status bonus to your Deception check equal to your extra damage from Arcane Cascade (typically 1, increasing to 2 if you have weapon specialization and 3 if you have greater weapon specialization).

items.name: Emergency Targe
items.summary: You immediately Raise a Shield or cast shield.
items.description:
**Trigger** An enemy you're aware of hits you with a Strike or a spell attack, or you fail a save against an enemy's spell.

**Requirements** You are wielding a shield or have the Shield spell prepared.

You immediately Raise a Shield or cast *shield*. The circumstance bonus applies to your defenses when determining the outcome of the triggering attack or spell.

items.name: Exploding Bullet
items.summary: You load your gun with a bullet forged of magic instead of matter, barely contained in an arcane shell.
items.description:
**Requirements** You're wielding an unloaded firearm.

You load your gun with a bullet forged of magic instead of matter, barely contained in an arcane shell. Interact to reload your firearm, creating an arcane round made from your choice of fire or sonic energy. When you shoot this round, the Strike gains the arcane trait and the corresponding energy trait. The firearm gains the scatter 5 feet trait, or gains a +1 status bonus to its splash damage if it already has the scatter trait. The scatter trait's splash damage uses the energy type you chose. The bullet disappears if not fired by the end of your next turn.

If your firearm takes more than 1 action to reload, you need to use Exploding Bullet for all the actions needed to reload it to get the benefits.

**Special** When you use volatile spark's Reloading Cascade action, you can use Exploding Bullet instead of an Interact action to reload a firearm.

items.name: Recharging Flurry
items.summary: The clash of steel fuels your magic, preparing you to unleash another magic-infused assault.
items.description:
**Requirements** You're wielding two melee weapons, each in a different hand.

The clash of steel fuels your magic, preparing you to unleash another magic-infused assault. Make one Strike with each of your weapons, then recharge your Spellstrike (regardless of whether the Strikes hit). Your multiple attack penalty increases after each Strike as normal. If the second Strike targets a creature you haven't attacked yet this turn, its multiple attack penalty is –4 if it's your second attack this turn (–3 if you're using an agile weapon) or –8 if it's your third or further Strike (–6 with an agile weapon).

items.name: Running Recharge
items.summary: Preparing in every way for your next assault, you both relocate yourself and ready your Spellstrike.
items.description: Preparing in every way for your next assault, you both relocate yourself and ready your Spellstrike. You recharge your Spellstrike and either Stride up to half your Speed or Step.

items.name: Starlit Eyes
items.summary: Starlight shines in your sight, enhancing your perception and range.
items.description:
Starlight shines in your sight, enhancing your perception and range.

When you make a ranged Strike, you lower the DC of your flat check to target a creature that's concealed or hidden from you. The DC is reduced to 4 instead of 5 against a concealed creature and to 10 instead of 11 against a hidden one. If you're in Arcane Cascade stance, you instead reduce the DC to 3 against a concealed creature or 9 against a hidden one.

In addition, when you cast Shooting Star and target a hidden creature, you don't have to attempt the flat check for targeting a hidden creature with a ranged Strike.

items.name: Steady Spellcasting (Magus)
items.summary: Confident in your technique, you don't easily lose your concentration when you Cast a Spell.
items.description:
Confident in your technique, you don't easily lose your concentration when you Cast a Spell.

If another creature's reaction would disrupt your spellcasting action, attempt a DC 15 flat. If you succeed, your action isn't disrupted.

items.name: Striker's Scroll
items.summary: You can attach a scroll to your weapon or Handwraps of Mighty Blows to blend its spell into an attack, carefully folding it around a part of the weapon or sealing it to the weapon's surface.
items.description:
You can attach a scroll to your weapon or Handwraps of Mighty Blows to blend its spell into an attack, carefully folding it around a part of the weapon or sealing it to the weapon's surface. Attaching a scroll requires using the Affix a Talisman action. You can have only one scroll affixed to a weapon at a time, and you can't have both a talisman and scroll attached.

You can Cast the Spell from the scroll as part of a Spellstrike, provided the spell is one you could normally use with Spellstrike. You can't Cast the Spell in any other way while it's affixed, though you can use Affix a Talisman again to remove the scroll and use it as a normal—if a bit crumpled—scroll.

items.name: Student of the Staff
items.prerequisites: Arcane Cascade; twisting tree hybrid study
items.summary: You've studied the staff extensively to learn the hidden capabilities of your chosen weapon.
items.description:
You've studied the staff extensively to learn the hidden capabilities of your chosen weapon. When you critically succeed at an attack roll using a staff, you can apply the critical specialization effect of the club group. (If you use the critical specialization on a Spellstrike, the spell still affects the target even if you pushed the target out of reach.)

While you're in Arcane Cascade stance, your staff gains the deadly d6 trait, with the damage from the deadly die being the same damage type as the extra damage from Arcane Cascade.

In addition, you can place property runes into a magic staff you prepare, even though a magic staff can't typically hold property runes. You must first inscribe the property runes into your spellbook, using the same process as transferring a rune. The rune takes the form of a specialized diagram in your spellbook, occupying one page. You can't inscribe runes that can't be placed on a non-magical staff, nor can you inscribe the Shifting rune. When you prepare a staff, you can impart any number of property runes from your spellbook into the staff, up to the limit imposed by the staff's *weapon potency* rune.
items.cite: Impossible Magic — Feats: Student of the Staff

items.name: Conjurer's Countermeasure
items.summary: You can make yourself resistant to damaging spells.
items.description: You can make yourself resistant to damaging spells. You learn the Conjurer's Countermeasure conflux spell.

items.name: Knowledge is Power
items.summary: When you critically succeed at a Recall Knowledge check about a creature, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to your next attack roll against the creature, to your AC against its next attack roll, and…
items.description:
When you critically succeed at a Recall Knowledge check about a creature, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to your next attack roll against the creature, to your AC against its next attack roll, and to your save against its next effect requiring a save.

If you share this information with your allies, they gain the benefits as well. If not used, these bonuses end after 1 minute.
items.cite: Impossible Magic — Feats: Knowledge is Power

items.name: Shielded Tome
items.summary: You can magically fuse a shield into your favorite book during your daily preparations or as a 10-minute activity with the manipulate trait.
items.description:
You can magically fuse a shield into your favorite book during your daily preparations or as a 10-minute activity with the manipulate trait. The shield appears in the book as an elaborate bookmark. The fusion lasts until you fuse a shield into a new book or the book is out of your possession for 24 hours. While the two are fused, the book shares the Hardness, Hit Points, and Broken Threshold of the shield.

The fused item has the shield's activations and benefits (such as a Spellguard Shield's bonus to saving throws against magic), and it can still be consulted as normal for purposes like Recall Knowledge and the benefits of Raise a Tome.

If the shield or your spellbook is etched with a *reinforcing* rune, the fused item gains the rune while they're fused; if both have the rune, the highest-level rune applies.

items.name: Spell Crash
items.summary: Instead of blending a spell into an attack, you can funnel the spell's magic into a pure blast that expands out from you.
items.description:
**Requirements** Your Spellstrike is charged, and you have at least one spell prepared in a spell slot.

Instead of blending a spell into an attack, you can funnel the spell's magic into a pure blast that expands out from you. You smash your weapon or fist into the ground and expend a spell prepared in one of your spell slots. The magic of the spell explodes out in your choice of a 20-foot emanation, 30-foot cone, or 60-foot line. Each creature in the area takes 1d10 force damage per spell rank of the expended spell, with a basic basic Reflex save against your spell DC. If your weapon has the shove trait, you push any creature that fails its save 10 feet; if your weapon has the trip trait, any creature that fails its save falls prone. Your Spellstrike is no longer charged.

If the spell you expended could deal a type of damage other than force, you can change the explosion's damage to that type and replace Spell Crash's force trait with the corresponding trait.

items.name: Spell Retaliation
items.summary: Battling other spellcasters is one of your major focuses, and harnessing magic from spells you defend against gives you everything you need to fight back.
items.description:
**Requirements** Your Spellstrike isn't charged.

**Trigger** You succeed at a saving throw against an enemy's spell, or an enemy fails a spell attack roll against you.

Battling other spellcasters is one of your major focuses, and harnessing magic from spells you defend against gives you everything you need to fight back. You recharge your Spellstrike.

items.name: Capture Magic
items.summary: When you resist a spell, you capture some of its magic for your own use.
items.description:
**Trigger** You succeed at your save against an enemy's harmful spell, or an enemy fails a spell attack roll against you from a harmful spell.

When you resist a spell, you capture some of its magic for your own use. You enter your Arcane Cascade stance, using the triggering spell to determine what damage type your Arcane Cascade deals.

Alternatively, if you're already in Arcane Cascade, you can instead amplify its effects temporarily. Until the end of your next turn, you gain a +2 status bonus to the extra damage and resistance you gain from your Arcane Cascade.

items.name: Fused Staff
items.summary: You can use your arcane prowess to fuse a magical staff into a weapon during your daily preparations or as a 10-minute activity with the manipulate trait.
items.description:
You can use your arcane prowess to fuse a magical staff into a weapon during your daily preparations or as a 10-minute activity with the manipulate trait. The fusion lasts until you fuse the staff again or the weapon is out of your possession for 24 hours. The fused item has the staff's activations and other benefits, and it can be used to cast spells if you prepare it. The staff and the weapon share their fundamental runes, using whichever *weapon potency* and whichever *striking* rune is higher level. If the staff has property runes, they're suppressed while it's fused.

The item's fused abilities work for you alone. A different wielder can use the weapon normally, but they don't get the benefit of the shared runes and can't use the staff's spells or abilities.

items.name: Runic Impression
items.summary: You can temporarily replicate the effects of a property rune for your weapon or unarmed attacks.
items.description: You can temporarily replicate the effects of a property rune for your weapon or unarmed attacks. You learn the Runic Impression conflux spell.

items.name: Spell Swipe
items.summary: You attack in an arc and enact your spell against everyone you hit.
items.description:
**Requirements** Your Spellstrike is charged.

You attack in an arc and enact your spell against everyone you hit. Make a Spellstrike, but roll separate Strikes to attack two creatures, each of whom must be within your melee reach and adjacent to each other. If your spell could affect two or more targets or would normally have an area, your spell affects whichever foes you hit, not just the first target; otherwise, choose one target to affect with the spell. As Spellstrike, Spell Swipe counts as two attacks for your multiple attack penalty, but the penalty doesn't increase until after you make both attacks.

If you're using a weapon that has the sweep trait, its circumstance bonus applies against both targets. You can use this activity with only melee Strikes, even if you have the starlit span hybrid study or a similar ability.

If you use Expansive Spellstrike to Spellstrike with an area spell, apply the area as described in Expansive Spellstrike, choosing one of the two targets to determine the area.

items.name: Standby Spell
items.summary: You've honed one spell as your favored combat technique, and you've practiced it enough that you no longer need to prepare it to cast it.
items.description: You've honed one spell as your favored combat technique, and you've practiced it enough that you no longer need to prepare it to cast it. Choose a spell in your spellbook that you could use with Spellstrike and that has a rank no higher than the highest-rank magus spell slot you have. You can cast this spell without having it prepared ahead of time by expending a spell slot of a sufficient rank to cast your chosen spell. You can change this spell whenever you add new spells to your spellbook, or by studying your spellbook for 1 hour.

items.name: Cascading Ray
items.summary: Magical energy spills out to extend beyond the creature you struck.
items.description:
**Requirements** Your last action was a successful Spellstrike, and the spell you cast dealt energy damage (acid, cold, electricity, fire, force, sonic, vitality, or void).

Magical energy spills out to extend beyond the creature you struck. The flowing energy forms a ray with a range of 120 feet originating from the creature you damaged. You can't target any of the creatures you damaged with your Spellstrike with the ray. Make a spell attack against the new target's AC, at the same multiple attack penalty as the Strike. On a hit, the target of the ray takes 1d4 damage per spell rank of the spell you used for Spellstrike, or 1d8 damage per rank if you cast the spell from a spell slot. The ray uses the same damage type as the spell dealt (choose one if it dealt more than one type of damage). This ray has the attack trait, the tradition trait of the original spell, and the trait matching the damage type.

items.name: Dazzling Block
items.summary: As your shield blocks an assault, you create a flash of brilliant, multicolored light in a 15-foot cone.
items.description:
**Trigger** You use Shield Block.

As your shield blocks an assault, you create a flash of brilliant, multicolored light in a 15-foot cone. Each creature in the area must attempt a Fortitude save against your spell DC, with the following effects.

**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.

**Success** The creature is dazzled for 1 round.

**Failure** The creature is blinded for 1 round and dazzled for 1 minute. The creature can spend an Interact action rubbing its eyes to end this blinded condition.

**Critical Failure** The creature is blinded for 1 round and dazzled for 1 hour.

items.name: Dimensional Disappearance
items.prerequisites: dimensional assault focus spell; laughing shadow hybrid study
items.summary: You take advantage of certain idiosyncrasies of teleportation magic to better hide your position.
items.description:
You take advantage of certain idiosyncrasies of teleportation magic to better hide your position. When you cast Dimensional Assault, you're affected by an Invisibility spell at the end of the teleport.

You can choose not to make the Strike that is normally part of *dimensional assault*. If you do make the Strike, your *invisibility* ends after the Strike, as normal for *invisibility*.

items.name: Killshot's Report
items.summary: As you drop an enemy, a loud echo issues out as you chain the spell's energy to a nearby creature.
items.description:
**Requirements** Your Spellstrike reduces an enemy to 0 HP.

As you drop an enemy, a loud echo issues out as you chain the spell's energy to a nearby creature. Choose a secondary target within 10 feet of the creature you reduced to 0 HP. This secondary target is affected by the spell you used for your Spellstrike. The creature gets any defense against the spell that Spellstrike normally allows, and you use your Strike result for a spell attack roll if needed. If the secondary target was already affected by the spell in some way (in the area of an Expansive Spellstrike, for example), it can't be affected a second time.

items.name: Lunging Spellstrike
items.summary: Your spell unwinds the structure of your staff to make it exceptionally long, or even separate it into shards held together by magical power.
items.description:
**Requirements** You’re wielding a staff.

Your spell unwinds the structure of your staff to make it exceptionally long, or even separate it into shards held together by magical power.

Make a Spellstrike with a staff, with a spell that isn’t a cantrip or focus spell. Increase the staff’s reach by 5 feet × the spell’s rank.

items.name: Meteoric Spellstrike
items.summary: A trail of energy flows from your target back to you.
items.description:
**Requirements** You're wielding a ranged or thrown weapon, or have a ranged unarmed attack.

A trail of energy flows from your target back to you. Make a Spellstrike with a ranged weapon or ranged unarmed attack against a target within the ranged weapon or unarmed attack's first range increment. The spell you cast for the Spellstrike can't be a cantrip or focus spell. Each creature in a line between you and the target, excluding you and the target, takes damage equal to double the spell's rank. Determine the damage type as described in Arcane Cascade.

items.name: Rapid Recharge
items.summary: You tap into an arcane trick to recover your ability to meld spells and attacks.
items.description:
**Frequency** once per day

You tap into an arcane trick to recover your ability to meld spells and attacks. You recharge your Spellstrike.

items.name: Split Spellstrike
items.summary: Like knives slicing through magic itself, both your weapons carry your spell, delivering it to separate foes.
items.description:
**Requirements** You're wielding two melee weapons, each in a different hand, and your Spellstrike is charged.

Like knives slicing through magic itself, both your weapons carry your spell, delivering it to separate foes. Make a Spellstrike with a spell that can target at least 2 creatures or that has an area. You can make two melee Strikes instead of one, but each must be made with a different weapon and target a different creature. Increase your multiple attack penalty normally after each Strike rather than increasing it for Spellstrike as a whole. If you're in Arcane Cascade, you can apply twofold tine's extra benefit between the two Strikes.

items.name: Sustaining Steel
items.summary: You pull magic from the surrounding area into your weapon, using its substance to transform the magic into restorative energy.
items.description:
**Trigger** You Cast a Spell using a spell slot.

You pull magic from the surrounding area into your weapon, using its substance to transform the magic into restorative energy. You regain Hit Points equal to the triggering spell's rank and roll to end any persistent void damage you have. If you're in the Arcane Cascade stance, the healing is equal to double the spell's rank.

If the spell had the vitality or void trait, any persistent vitality or void damage you have ends automatically, and you can change the damage type from Arcane Cascade to vitality or void if you wish. (Vitality damage typically damages only undead or other creatures with void healing.)

items.name: Conflux Focus
items.summary: You imagine how you'll weave magic and combat into future battles, improving your focus.
items.description: You imagine how you'll weave magic and combat into future battles, improving your focus. Whenever you Refocus, you completely refill your focus pool.

items.name: Magic Sense (Magus)
items.summary: You can sense the presence of magic auras as though you were always using a 1st-rank Detect Magic spell.
items.description: You can sense the presence of magic auras as though you were always using a 1st-rank Detect Magic spell. This detects magic in your field of vision only. When you Seek, you gain the benefits of a 3rd-rank *detect magic* spell on things you see (in addition to the normal benefits of Seeking). You can turn this sense off and on with a free action at the start or the end of your turn.

items.name: Overwhelming Spellstrike
items.summary: You pierce through your foe's resistance.
items.description:
**Requirements** Your Spellstrike is charged.

You pierce through your foe's resistance. Make a Spellstrike. The spell you cast as part of the Spellstrike ignores an amount of the target's resistance to acid, cold, electricity, fire, or sonic damage equal to your level. This applies to all damage the spell deals, including persistent damage and damage caused by an ongoing effect of the spell. A creature's immunities are unaffected.

items.name: Sprinting Spellstrike
items.summary: Magic propels you across the battlefield as you speed toward your target.
items.description:
**Requirements** Your Spellstrike is charged.

Magic propels you across the battlefield as you speed toward your target. Make a Spellstrike, casting a spell that has a line area. Before making your Strike, you Stride in a straight line to a distance up to the line's length; you can move through enemies during this movement, and your movement doesn't trigger reactions. You can use Sprinting Spellstrike while Burrowing, Climbing, Flying, or Swimming instead of Striding if you have the corresponding movement type.

**Special** If you have the Expansive Spellstrike feat, the spell's area uses the line of your movement instead of the normal method of determining the line.

items.name: Arcane Shroud
items.summary: Your magic has a powerful aftereffect, briefly granting you a certain spell.
items.description:
Your magic has a powerful aftereffect, briefly granting you a certain spell. When you take this feat, choose three of False Vitality, Fleet Step, Invisibility, Mountain Resilience, Resist Energy, and See the Unseen.

When you use Arcane Cascade, choose one of the spells you selected with this feat. You're affected by this aftereffect spell until the end of your next turn, though it ends early if the stance ends or another circumstance ends it (such as if you take a hostile action while affected by *invisibility*). If you're 18th level or higher, a *false vitality* or *resist energy* you get from Arcane Shroud is heightened to 4th rank.

**Special** You can select this feat a second time to add the remaining spells to your set of choices.

items.name: Hasted Assault
items.summary: You can speed yourself up to move and attack more swiftly.
items.description: You can speed yourself up to move and attack more swiftly. You learn the Hasted Assault conflux spell.

items.name: Preternatural Parry
items.summary: You snap your weapon or limb into place to ward off harm.
items.description:
**Trigger** You're targeted by a Strike or a spell attack, or you're about to roll a saving throw against a spell effect.

**Requirements** You have one or more hands free.

You snap your weapon or limb into place to ward off harm. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to AC and saving throws against the triggering effect until the start of your next turn.

items.name: Dispelling Spellstrike
items.summary: The spell you deliver tries to force out magic affecting your enemy.
items.description:
**Requirements** Your Spellstrike is charged.

The spell you deliver tries to force out magic affecting your enemy. Make a Spellstrike. If it hits, you also attempt to counteract a single spell of your choice that is active on the target.

The counteract rank is half your level rounded up, and the counteract check modifier is the standard modifier for counteracting with a spell (your Intelligence modifier plus your spellcasting proficiency bonus, plus any bonuses or penalties that specifically apply to counteract checks).

items.name: Resounding Cascade
items.summary: The magical reinforcement from your Arcane Cascade extends to nearby allies.
items.description:
The magical reinforcement from your Arcane Cascade extends to nearby allies. While you're in Arcane Cascade stance, you grant its extra damage and resistance in an aura affecting all allies in a 5-foot emanation. This uses only the base values of your stance; it doesn't use any increase you get from bonuses, the laughing shadow hybrid study, or the like.

As normal for duplicate effects, multiple Arcane Cascades affecting the same creature aren't cumulative.

items.name: Stolen Spell
items.summary: As you perfectly counter a spell, you re-aim its magic to use it yourself.
items.description:
**Trigger** You critically succeed at a saving throw against an enemy's spell, or an enemy critically fails a spell attack roll against you.

As you perfectly counter a spell, you re-aim its magic to use it yourself. You gain the ability to cast the triggering spell one time before the end of your next turn, even if it's not on your spell list or is of a higher rank than you can cast. This doesn't cost you a spell slot or other resource. If you cast it as part of a Spellstrike against the creature that originally cast it, that creature is off-guard against your Strike. Use your own spellcasting statistics for this spell, as you do for other spells you cast.

items.name: Versatile Spellstrike
items.summary: You can channel the entire realm of possibilities of your spellbook into an attack.
items.description:
You can channel the entire realm of possibilities of your spellbook into an attack.

Once during your daily preparations, you can use a spell slot to hold that infinite potential, rather than using it to prepare a spell. When you make a Spellstrike, you can expend this special spell slot to immediately prepare and cast a spell from your spellbook at 2 ranks lower than the slot's rank. (As normal for preparing spells, you can use a spell of an even lower rank, heightening it accordingly.)

You don't have any spell prepared in that slot until you cast from that slot.

items.name: Supreme Spellstrike
items.summary: For you, it is almost effortless to combine spells and attacks into devastating combinations.
items.description: For you, it is almost effortless to combine spells and attacks into devastating combinations. You're permanently quickened. You can use your extra action only to Strike or to recharge Spellstrike.

items.name: Whirlwind Spell
items.summary: You combine the might of a multitarget spell with a whirling flurry of attacks.
items.description:
**Requirements** Your Spellstrike is charged.

You combine the might of a multitarget spell with a whirling flurry of attacks. You use Spellstrike, making a melee Strike against each enemy within your reach instead of against one enemy. If your spell can affect multiple targets or normally has an area, your spell affects all foes you hit, not just the first target, up to the spell's normal maximum targets. If you Strike more enemies than the spell could target, choose which foes are affected by the spell. Each attack counts toward your multiple attack penalty but doesn't increase your penalty until you've made all your attacks.

You can use this activity with only melee Strikes, even if you have the starlit span hybrid study or a similar ability.

If you use Expansive Spellstrike to Spellstrike with an area spell, apply the area as described in Expansive Spellstrike, choosing one of the targets to determine the area.

items.name: Death Speaker
items.summary: Your voice and magic speak to the core existence within undead creatures, circumventing the need for the creature to comprehend.
items.description: Your voice and magic speak to the core existence within undead creatures, circumventing the need for the creature to comprehend. Your spells and abilities ignore the mindless trait and any immunity to emotion, fear, or mental effects when targeting or affecting undead creatures. Additionally, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus when you attempt to Make An Impression on and make a Request of an undead creature.

items.name: Reach of the Dead
items.summary: You channel your necrotic magic through a thrall, expending it in the process.
items.description: You channel your necrotic magic through a thrall, expending it in the process. If the next action you use is to Cast a Spell that has range, you cast that spell from one of your thralls within 60 feet. That thrall becomes the point of origin for your spell; calculate range and cover from its space instead of yours. The thrall is then destroyed.
items.cite: Impossible Magic — Feats: Reach of the Dead

items.name: The Hallowed Dead
items.summary: While many necromancers seek unholy and perverse power, you have dedicated yourself to the practice of necromancy to stop the creation of permanent undead and the corruption of souls.
items.description: While many necromancers seek unholy and perverse power, you have dedicated yourself to the practice of necromancy to stop the creation of permanent undead and the corruption of souls. You and your thralls gain the holy trait. Strikes your thralls make gain the holy trait and deal 1 additional spirit damage. This additional spirit damage increases to 2 at 10th level. You also gain the following anathema: "purposefully create undead to do undue harm."
items.cite: Impossible Magic — Feats: The Hallowed Dead

items.name: The Unholy Dead
items.summary: You have turned your necromancy against the divine powers that seek to stop you from achieving your unholy goals.
items.description: You have turned your necromancy against the divine powers that seek to stop you from achieving your unholy goals. You and your thralls gain the unholy trait. Strikes your thralls make gain the unholy trait and deal 1 additional spirit damage. This additional spirit damage increases to 2 at 10th level. You also gain the following anathema: "destroy undead of no harm to you."
items.cite: Impossible Magic — Feats: The Unholy Dead

items.name: Undead Familiar
items.summary: You gain the ability to raise an undead familiar who will serve you as your loyal and sometimes expendable partner as you explore your necromantic magic.
items.description: You gain the ability to raise an undead familiar who will serve you as your loyal and sometimes expendable partner as you explore your necromantic magic. You gain a familiar. It has the undead trait instead of the animal trait and is immune to bleed, death effects, disease, mental, and poison. You can choose only one familiar ability per day for this familiar instead of two, and you can't choose an ability that changes the creature's trait (such as construct or dragon). Additionally, this familiar can be targeted by spells and abilities that target your thralls. If you destroy your familiar, you can raise them back to undeath during your next daily preparations.

items.name: Widespread Fascination
items.summary: You are not content to restrict yourself to one field.
items.description:
You are not content to restrict yourself to one field. Instead, you've studied a wider range of necromantic magic to better expand your horizons and explore your unscrupulous fascinations. You learn the grave spell for a Grim Fascination other than yours. You must have access to that fascination. Access can be gained from independent study or sought-out tutelage.

**Special** You can select this feat more than once, choosing a different grave spell each time.

items.name: Bone Speaker
items.summary: To truly understand the mechanical advantages of an undead skeleton, you must understand how it functioned in life.
items.description:
To truly understand the mechanical advantages of an undead skeleton, you must understand how it functioned in life. You can Recall Knowledge on living creatures with an internal or external skeleton using Undead Lore. If you do, you can learn only information pertaining to the biology of a creature—not any learned abilities or abilities granted by items.

Additionally, you can perform a forensic examination on a corpse using Undead Lore instead of Medicine if the corpse came from a creature with a skeleton.

items.name: Deathly Scream
items.summary: A thrall's scream mentally harms and frightens your foes.
items.description: A thrall's scream mentally harms and frightens your foes. You learn the Deathly Scream grave spell.

items.name: Draining Strike
items.summary: You draw the life out of your target using both your weapon and your thralls as a conduit.
items.description:
**Frequency** once per turn

You draw the life out of your target using both your weapon and your thralls as a conduit. Make a Strike. This counts as two attacks when calculating your multiple attack penalty. On a success, you can destroy a thrall that is within 10 feet of you or your target to have your Strike deal an additional 1d6 spirit damage. You regain Hit Points equal to the spirit damage dealt.

At 10th and 18th level, you can destroy up to one additional thrall as part of this action to deal an additional 1d6 damage for each additional thrall destroyed.

items.name: Enhanced Undead Familiar
items.summary: You infuse your undead familiar with void energy.
items.description: You infuse your undead familiar with void energy. You can select three familiar or master abilities each day, instead of one.
items.cite: Impossible Magic — Feats: Enhanced Undead Familiar

items.name: Invert Harm
items.summary: Your mastery of life and death grows.
items.description: Your mastery of life and death grows. When you cast Harm, it can heal living creatures as though they were undead.

items.name: Muscle Barrier
items.summary: You create an extra thick layer of muscle to protect your target.
items.description: You create an extra thick layer of muscle to protect your target. You learn the Muscle Barrier grave spell.

items.name: Song of the Soul
items.summary: You transform a thrall into a special instrument that plays a silent, soothing song heard only by a creature's soul.
items.description: You transform a thrall into a special instrument that plays a silent, soothing song heard only by a creature's soul. You learn the Song of the Soul grave spell.
items.cite: Impossible Magic — Feats: Song of the Soul

items.name: Undead Creator
items.summary: You've learned the unholy art of creating permanent undead creatures.
items.description: You've learned the unholy art of creating permanent undead creatures. You learn the Create Undead ritual. You can cast this ritual without a secondary caster. When you do, you must fulfill any requirements for the secondary caster, and you attempt the secondary check normally performed by that secondary caster.

items.name: Body Shield
items.summary: You throw an adjacent thrall in between you and the attacker.
items.description:
**Trigger** A creature targets you with an attack, and you can see the attacker.

**Requirements** You are adjacent to at least one of your thralls.

You throw an adjacent thrall in between you and the attacker. The thrall grants you a +2 circumstance bonus to AC against the triggering attack. If the attack still hits, you gain resistance to the triggering attack's damage equal to your level. Regardless of the result, the thrall is destroyed.

items.name: Bony Barrage
items.summary: You launch a massive barrage of tiny bones.
items.description: You launch a massive barrage of tiny bones. You learn the Bony Barrage grave spell.

items.name: Ghostly Stride
items.summary: You fade into a slightly incorporeal form as you move.
items.description: You fade into a slightly incorporeal form as you move. You Stride up to half your Speed. This movement doesn't trigger reactions, and you can move through enemies' spaces during it. If you have a fly Speed, you can instead Fly up to half your fly Speed.

items.name: Mobile Thralls
items.summary: Your thralls can now follow you wherever you go.
items.description:
Your thralls can now follow you wherever you go. Any thrall you create has your choice of a climb Speed or swim Speed. The additional Speed is equal to its land Speed, and any time you let the thrall Stride, you can have it use the relevant movement action instead.

At 8th level, add a fly Speed to your choices. A flying thrall remains airborne at the end of your turn even if it didn't Fly that turn.

items.name: Osteo Armaments
items.summary: If you have bones, you have a weapon.
items.description:
If you have bones, you have a weapon. You create a *+1 striking* weapon in which you are proficient, made of bone and sinew. If this weapon requires ammunition, mundane bone ammunition is created when you reload it. The weapon falls apart and is destroyed after 1 hour, if you aren't holding the weapon at the end of your turn, or if you use this action again, whichever comes first.

At 8th level, you can destroy an adjacent thrall as part of using this action. If you do, the action gains the thrall trait and the weapon also gains a *Decaying rune*, or the *Greater decaying rune* if you're 15th level or higher.

At 10th level, the weapon improves to a *+2 striking* weapon, increasing to a *+2 greater striking* weapon at 12th level, a *+3 greater striking* weapon at 16th level, or a *+3 major striking* weapon at 19th level.

Effect: Osteo Armaments

items.name: Overwhelming Harm
items.summary: Your ability to manipulate void energy has led you to the conclusion that more is always better.
items.description: Your ability to manipulate void energy has led you to the conclusion that more is always better. Whenever you cast the 3-action version of Harm, you can extend the area to a 60-foot emanation.

items.name: Vampiric Spell
items.summary: Your magic drains the life from your enemy.
items.description: Your magic drains the life from your enemy. If the next action you use is to Cast a Spell that deals damage, you gain temporary Hit Points equal to half the initial damage a single creature takes from this spell; calculate these temporary Hit Points using the creature that took the most damage from the spell. These temporary Hit Points last for 1 minute.

items.name: Void Siphon (Necromancer)
items.summary: You open your body to absorb void energy.
items.description:
**Trigger** You would take void damage.

**Requirements** You are living.

You open your body to absorb void energy. You gain resistance equal to your level to the triggering void damage. After you take the triggering damage, you gain temporary Hit Points equal to your level. These temporary Hit Points last for 1 round.

items.name: Bind Heroic Spirit
items.summary: You bind the spirit of a dead hero into you, gaining some of their talent.
items.description: You bind the spirit of a dead hero into you, gaining some of their talent. You learn the Bind Heroic Spirit grave spell.
items.cite: Impossible Magic — Feats: Bind Heroic Spirit

items.name: Bloody Tendrils
items.summary: You create three immobile tendrils made of blood that lash out at your enemies.
items.description: You create three immobile tendrils made of blood that lash out at your enemies. You learn the Bloody Tendrils grave spell.

items.name: Bone Burst
items.summary: You destroy the thrall in an explosion of bone shards that fly toward the triggering creature, dealing level-based piercing damage with a basic Reflex save against your spell DC.
items.description:
**Trigger** A creature adjacent to one of your thralls uses a manipulate action or a move action, makes a ranged attack, or leaves a square during a move action it's using, and you are within 30 feet of the thrall.

You destroy the thrall in an explosion of bone shards that fly toward the triggering creature, dealing level-based piercing damage with a basic Reflex save against your spell DC.

The damage increases to 3d10 at 12th and to 4d10 at 18th level.

items.name: Collateral Reinforcement
items.summary: With a combination of bony armor, extra flesh layers, and tactical incorporeal phasing, you protect your thralls from collateral damage.
items.description: With a combination of bony armor, extra flesh layers, and tactical incorporeal phasing, you protect your thralls from collateral damage. For 1 round, your thralls become immune to area and splash damage.

items.name: Conjurer of Corpses
items.summary: You can call forth many kinds of undead to do your bidding.
items.description: You can call forth many kinds of undead to do your bidding. You learn the Summon Undead spell. Undead creatures you summon with this spell can be destroyed and targeted by your spells or abilities as if they were thralls. You gain an additional spell slot each day at your highest rank of necromancer spell slots. You can prepare only the *summon undead* spell in this slot.
items.cite: Impossible Magic — Feats: Conjurer of Corpses

items.name: Corrupted Ground
items.traits: aura, concentrate, necromancer, occult, spirit, unholy, void
items.summary: The ground on which you stride is mere fuel that you burn with unholy void energies, scarring the earth in your wake.
items.description: The ground on which you stride is mere fuel that you burn with unholy void energies, scarring the earth in your wake. When a holy creature or psychopomp ends its turn within 10 feet of you, it takes level-based spirit damage. If it's a holy living creature, it takes an additional level-based void damage. At 10th level and every 4 levels thereafter, the spirit and void damage each increase by 2. Corrupted Ground lasts for 1 minute, but you can Dismiss it.

items.name: Hallowed Earth
items.traits: aura, concentrate, holy, necromancer, occult, spirit, vitality
items.summary: The earth is both where the dead rise from and where they are put to rest.
items.description: The earth is both where the dead rise from and where they are put to rest. Your presence sanctifies the earth around you. When an unholy creature ends its turn within 10 feet of you, it takes level-based spirit damage. If it's an unholy undead creature, it takes an additional level-based vitality damage. At 10th level and every 4 levels thereafter, the spirit and vitality damage each increase by 2. Hallowed Earth lasts for 1 minute, but you can Dismiss it.

items.name: Reclaim Power
items.summary: You use your thralls to restore yourself.
items.description:
**Frequency** once per 10 minutes
